title: Good value as general use PC; Much faster with 16GB ram
text:
Overall, I've been quite happy with this purchase. I bought it a year and a half ago, in July 2019, and the machine has been working well for me since then. I upgraded the 4GB RAM to 16GB and it has performed significantly faster since then, although it was probably suitable for an average user with the pre-installed 4GB. I also added a 2TB HDD for storing media; the pre-installed 128GB SDD is extremely fast but did not provide enough space for photos, videos, or large apps.

PROS
+ Keyboard - The keyboard feels good and is easy to type fast on, and includes the numeric keypad on the side which is helpful. Also the backlit keys use very helpful when ambient light is low.
+ Screen - Screen is sufficiently bright, and while it will not rival a new Apple monitor, I think it's quite good for the price point.
+ 3 USB ports - Helpful for quickly connecting accessories
+ Aesthetics - Looks nice!

CONS
+ Trackpad - It gets in the way. When I'm trying to type the cursor suddenly moves. The solution I've found is hit F7 which disables the trackpad, and use an external mouse. This works great when I'm at a desk and the trackpad isn't a problem.
+ May need upgrade of RAM and HDD/SDD - While the 4GB RAM and 128GB SDD are sufficient for basic web browsing and word processing, if you are a power user or close to it, you'll certainly need to upgrade the RAM and drive to provide greater capacity. Good news is you can easily do so, and at a low cost.

title: Bang for your Buck... but two minor issues
text:
This is my first laptop, so keep in mind that I know nothing about laptops.

However, I got this laptop for animation purposes. A creative whim to see if OpenToonz is as great as two hundred Youtubers swear it is.
I was worried that it might not be able to handle such complex programs, since it is in fact a budget laptop, but I was pleasantly surprised. Not only does it effectively run OpenToonz, it also handles rendering in Blender and other programs that I thought might be too much for its processing capacity. I've played a few high resolution games on it without any issues, as well.

I saw another review from a wonderful human being who knows a lot more about computers than me, and he left in depth instructions on how to turn off S Mode as well as how to upgrade your computer with a couple additional parts to expand its memory and processing. I did not utilize any of those recommendations (yet) and the laptop works amazing!
It's got super fast internet, downloads everything quickly, amazing resolution, and like I said, it can handle some pretty tough programs. Some of my friends can't run blender on their own laptops, so that speaks for itself.

Still, there are two issues I've found so far.

Issue 1, the most obvious:
The volume on this laptop is crap. It can be sitting right in front of your face and not be loud enough for you to hear the quieter sounds in a video. This is easy to fix with a speaker, so it's not a big deal, but I'd recommend getting a speaker at the same time you get the laptop just to avoid the disappointment when movie time comes around.

Issue 2:
It overheats very very VERY easily. Don't set this laptop on any blankets or pillows, or anything other than a hard surface.
I noticed quickly that it gets warm basically as soon as you set it down on your lap, so I've been pretty careful about that. But just earlier today, I fell asleep with it on my lap (oops) and when I woke up about an hour later, it was off. It would not turn on. The charging light was blue, meaning that it was charging properly from the cord. When I pressed the power button, however, the power light flashed blue one time very briefly but the laptop didn't even try to turn on. No fans, no clicks, nothing. I waited an hour and tried again, but it still wouldn't turn on. Needless to say, I was horrified!
If this happens to you, please don't panic, it's very easy to fix.
Windows laptops have this handy dandy feature where they shut themselves off if they're at risk of overheating, to prevent any damage from happening. They also prevent themselves from being turned back on, apparently, but you can fix it in three easy steps.

1: Unplug your computer from the power cord.
2: Flip the computer over, and use a needle to press and hold the battery reset button located on the bottom for 5 seconds.
3: Wait ten full minutes, plug in your computer, and turn it on.

Mine booted up instantly when I did that, and I was deeply grateful for the feature that saved my laptop from my own relentless stupidity.

With that said, this is a fantastic laptop and it works great, but there are two purchases you should make right off the bat: buy a speaker/headphones, and buy a cooling pad. I also highly recommend buying a mouse; the track pad isn't bad or anything- mine works as well as any track pad I've ever used- but computers are always better with a mouse ;D

If you're considering this laptop, I'd say go for it. Just make sure that if you're buying it for a kid or anyone who has a habit of laying in bed with the laptop in their lap, you get them a cooling pad. Windows will probably prevent it from being damaged from overheating, but you can spare them the panic of a laptop that won't turn on and the struggle of finding a needle that fits the reset hole.

Happy browsing, everyone!

title: Great If You Know What You’re Buying
text:
Like many Acer products, this thing is an incredible deal! It’s not a gaming laptop, though you can play some very light, simple games as with almost any device. As a daily driver for any other tasks, it’s a fantastic choice.

The screen is far superior to anything else you’ll find in this price range as it’s not only 1080p but the viewing angles are wide and the quality of the picture is great. The backlit keyboard is possibly the only one of its kind in this price range. It’s pretty big, and because of this they even manage to fit a small numpad into the keyboard layout which is practically unheard of when it comes to notebooks. The chassis is mostly metal (aluminum?) which is durable, more likely to dent than break, and provides some function as a heat sink. The bottom is plastic, but it’s well-ventilated.

Personally, I’m more of a Linux and even Mac guy myself (I bought this for my girlfriend), but don’t let any of those other reviewers scare you away. It does start in Windows S Mode but you can just turn that off - it comes with the full version of Windows 10 Home edition with Office and all the bells and whistles. The software alone is worth over $100. And of course if you’re more like me, you can always put a Linux distro on it instead if you prefer.

The downsides are obvious, but they’re also not really downsides in my opinion - 4gb of RAM and 128gb of storage. The storage is NVME M.2, though, so it’s about as good as it gets aside from capacity. As far as the storage capacity and amount of memory, it’s pretty much made to be expanded. Acer even has their own videos to show you how. RAM is cheap, and the memory standard here is pretty good. Out of the box, though, you will quickly realize that the notorious resource hog known as Windows will gobble up just about all of it - if you are doing much or have more than one window open you will notice it taking a moment to respond to your actions. Again though, this is an easy and cheap upgrade to fix. With the storage, there’s an additional 2.5” SSD bay/bracket waiting for an additional drive to be added so you can keep the stock drive as your boot drive if you like and just add an extra one for storage. In my opinion, though, most people that aren’t gaming usually aren’t going to be downloading 70gb files and the 128gb drive should be enough space.

All in all, this thing is a steal. If you’re looking for a notebook for serious gaming or a lot of video editing, you’re gonna have to spend at least 3x the price of this and I’d even suggest a desktop if that works for you. I doubt you’d even be looking at anything near this price if that was your intention, though. Right? So if you’re looking for a computer to use for any other purpose, and especially if you don’t mind adding in some extra RAM and maybe a 2.5” SSD if you need more space, absolutely buy this. I can’t imagine how anyone could regret it.

title: Great value! Instructions for RAM and HDD SSD upgrade here
text:
Buy this computer if you need a really great, full HD screen and a capable computer to do surfing, microsoft office sort of tasks, watching netflix, etc. Becomes a snappy surfing and binge watching champion if you throw an extra 4gb of memory in it and another SDD for storing your files.

Installing a memory (RAM) upgrade is easy. You turn the computer over, remove several small screws and then gently but firmly pry off the bottom plate. You will see one RAM module already installed. Snap the additional one into the open slot. If connected correctly, you are done. No changes needed in BIOS.

Installing a 2.5 HDD or SSD is a more difficult process that I would not recommend to folks who have not done a computer build or PC repair before. At first glance it appears that you can just plug your SATA drive in and close up the computer. This is not the case! You need to unscrew the SATA controller board -- you will notice that it isn't connected to anything! You will see a tiny ribbon cable in the same spot. You need to pick up that cable and clip the end of the ribbon marked HDD into the connector on the SATA controller board by lifting the tiny beige clip on the SATA controller and hooking the prongs of the ribbon cable's end into the slot before snapping the beige clip into place. Plug in your drive to the SATA connector and place this whole assembly onto the plastic sheeting with the SATA controller lined up next to the open connector on the motherboard that is labelled HDD0 (very small label). Take the end of the ribbon cabled marked Motherboard and plug that into the HDD0 connector on the motherboard, using the clip as before. Then you will screw the drive into the two metal rails to keep it in place, and finally screw the SATA controller board into it's new spot. Make sure nothing is wiggling or loose, make sure the ribbon cable ends are snapped in and not floating around. Then close up the laptop case. WHEW. Then you need to boot into BIOS by tapping F2 while the computer is starting. Verify that you see your drive listed in HDD0. Proceed to boot into windows and use the windows Disk Management tool to format your new drive!

title: A great value laptop with some tradeoffs, but well worth the price.
text:
Not going to go into the specs on this, but I'm going to say that I REALLY like this computer!

Pros:

1. Full size keyboard with a number pad (I need this since I do a lot of work with Excel).

2. Backlit keyboard (I sometimes work in poorly lit areas and this works wonders).

3. Bluetooth (great for routing sound through my soundbar should I decide to do that in the future).

4. Not a touchscreen! While some prefer them, I am going from a touchscreen laptop to a non-touchscreen laptop. (I found it annoying that stray hairs or other things would cling to the screen and then I couldn't clean the screen off without opening 15 different things on my old one. So, I was happy to find a laptop that didn't have that feature, which I do not miss at all.)

5. Long battery life (6+ hours--this is going to be great for car trips when the travel restrictions end).

6. Processor and memory are able to make instantaneous calculations on a 25 MB Excel sheet (which is unusually large).

7. Very lightweight (this is going to be fun when I go through airports again as I'm the Dad carrying two car seats along with the backpack of tech).

8. Not made in China! If you're trying to boycott Chinese goods like I am because of Xi Jinping's lackluster response to COVID-19, rest assured that Acer is based out of Taiwan.

Cons:

1. Windows 10 S-mode restricts you from third party programs like Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox. If you want them, you have to permanently take your computer out of S-mode.

2. The processor fan is a bit louder than most others. This sort of thing doesn't bother me, but it does bother my wife, who also has an Acer Aspire 5.

3. The processor fan also has a tendency to run while the laptop is closed. I'm not sure why it needs to run while it's supposed to be idle, but oh well. This is another thing that doesn't bother me, but it seems a bit odd.

4. The battery is not a removable module like other laptops' batteries. If this is going to be a very long term solution like my last laptop (bought in 2013), I know I'm going to need to find a way to put in a new battery safely and without damaging the unit.

5. The speakers are a bit weak. I discovered this one day when I lost my phone and needed to use it for distance learning school videos for my third grader. I had it on full blast in a quiet room and it was difficult to understand at times. (It was inspiration enough for me to get a nearby friend to call my phone so I could find it was kicked underneath the couch.) If good quality speakers are important to you, this unit isn't for you. For me, it doesn't matter because I can live without the Windows 10 sound effects and I don't use it for entertainment.

title: HP Chromebook
text:
My husband is not "computer" oriented, and he only uses one for eMail, to read and print PDFs, to read the news and watch the occasional video. I have the "real" computer for bookkeeping, graphics and some other heavy lifting. His "laptop," as it were, was an inexpensive Windows model that couldn't be upgraded, except for security updates. It was cheap and he was happy. But it's slowed to a crawl. We've cleaned out files and unused apps, defragged, all the stuff, but it's reached its end time.

As he has a Pixel phone, this Chromebook seemed a great way to sync his world in a way he couldn't easily do before (reminder, he's not computer savvy). And so far so good. Again, not computer savvy, so he didn't set up the Chromebook. But he COULD have, I think. It only took a few minutes, once signed in with his Google eMail, it understood all his needs and he was ready to go.

If I would have given it up.

I LOVE this thing! It's fast. It's quiet because it has a solid state drive. The speaker quality is great. The screen images are crisp. The touchpad is attentive. The standby battery life lasts for a week. It's lightweight. And it's pretty.

You can't load many of the apps you'd expect. They aren't available in the Play Store. Facebook, Netflix, Hulu all have to be accessed through the web browser. That's fine, just go to the site once, sign in, then bookmark it to the favorites bar. Every time after, open browser, click, you're there. I was able to load Microsoft Word which my husband rarely uses, but just in case he needed it, why not. It's a mobile version of Word, not the full program, but it's pretty darned full.

For anyone in your world who doesn't particularly like a tablet, but prefers something with a keyboard (without traveling with an extra keyboard to go with a tablet), this is a simple, inexpensive and elegant choice.

I don't even need it and I want one for myself. But (sigh) it's time to turn it over to husband.

I'll report back if we run into any problems, although I'm not anticipating any. It's a recommend for sure.
